gap: No result ChatGPT got sets the heated 12V options side by side on the maker's own store. On redodopower.com today, the self-heating 12V 100Ah (100 W pads, heats below 32°F, stops at 41°F) costs $251.99. The same store sells a heated 12V 165Ah Group 31 with a 150 W pad for $449.99, about $2.73/Ah against $2.52/Ah for the 100Ah.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's answer and the result list. The answer already shows Redodo at $251.99, SOK SK12V100H at $369.00 and an unnamed 'Smart … self-heating' battery at $629.99. Power Queen's page, the only one cited, gives the 10 A heater-trigger minimum. The 100Ah price is therefore already in front of the shopper. Only the larger heated Redodo models and the cost per Ah are new. I could not open SOK, Battle Born, Renogy, Power Queen, Rich Solar, Temgo, PowerUrus or Vatrer today (HTTP 429/403/404 or an SSL error), so I have no verified rival prices to compare.
decides: This confirms the 100Ah price, but it does not settle the pick by itself. Redodo's self-heating 12V 100Ah is $251.99 today on the maker's store, the same figure ChatGPT showed, and the lowest heated 100Ah price in ChatGPT's own answer (SOK $369.00, 'Smart' $629.99; I could not verify those today). A shopper who needs more capacity and a heated cranking battery can step up to Redodo's heated 165Ah Group 31, 1,200 CCA, for $449.99. Rival prices need to be re-checked before the page claims Redodo is cheapest.
